content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore common text and character errors within XML Text, Characters, and Entities. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: Common Text and Character Errors matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about unescaped special characters, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson focuses on common text and character errors and the listed concepts: Unescaped special characters; Illegal characters; Incorrect character references; Encoding mismatches. XML processors enforce the syntax rules, while validation and application code can impose additional constraints.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Unescaped special characters; Illegal characters; Incorrect character references; Encoding mismatches; Unexpected whitespace changes. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Common Text and Character Errors
content_blocks.code: <message>Use < for less than, & for ampersand, and " for a quote.</message>
content_blocks.expected_output: Reserved markup characters are represented using the predefined entities or appropriate character references.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. Keep document structure separate from presentation, use consistent names, and verify assumptions with a small sample. If behavior depends on an XML processor or version, record it in the project documentation.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the sample to its exact starting state before each experiment. Change one element, attribute, expression, or constraint at a time, then compare the result with the expected behavior.
content_blocks.limitations: This snippet is an inspectable example, not an XML execution service. Validate it with a standards-compatible XML processor; feature support depends on the processor/version.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Distinguish well-formedness, schema validity, and application-level correctness; they are different checks.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small synthetic example that demonstrates “Unescaped special characters”. Then add one boundary case involving “Illegal characters”. Write down what should happen before testing, and record the exact output or processor message afterward.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a document is correct because it looks readable.
common_mistakes.why: Visual appearance does not prove well-formedness, schema validity, correct namespace handling, or application-level meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse and validate the document with the intended processor, then assert its meaning using a focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing specification features with processor support.
common_mistakes.why: A standard may define features that a specific runtime does not implement.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the version and feature support; test with the actual target processor.

common_mistakes.why: Missing values, wrong types, namespace differences, or boundary inputs can expose failures.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a valid case, an invalid case, and an edge case to the verification notes.
